messages:
Maria C: Handing off to @Ashwin for tonight (I’ll be offline after 00:30 PST). Leaving a short watchlist and a couple of action items. TL;DR: router latency spike during the 20:15 dedicated deploy, kv-cache evictions rising, scheduled prune-job runs at 03:00.

Ashwin R: Got it. I’ll take the bridge and pager. Can you list the quick playbook steps for 503s and cache-related latency?

Maria C: Sure — if you see 503s or 5xx on /v1/generate: 1) check router pods (namespace=inference): `kubectl get pods -n inference -l app=router` 2) tail logs: `kubectl logs -n inference <router-pod> -c router --since=10m` 3) if kv-cache evictions > 1000/min, add a temporary replica to cache pool (follow runbook).

Maria C: Copy of the quick commands:
```
# list router pods
kubectl get pods -n inference -l app=router
# describe node pressure
kubectl describe node ip-10-0-2-45
```

Lina S: FYI — the 20:15 dedicated rollout bumped p95 by ~120ms for ~8 mins (observed in console). We rolled back one canary after the spike. Watch for a recurrence around high traffic windows (21:00-21:30 PST). Also seeing kv-cache evictions trending up after the new model quantization change.

Jeff K: I’ll take watch for routing flaps. If we get increased 5xx > 0.8% for 5m, I’ll pause canary and ping infra. :thumbsup:

Ashwin R: Thanks — noted thresholds: 5xx > 0.8% for 5m, p95 increase > 100ms baseline. I have oncall-sla dashboard pinned. Also going to temporarily bump router-replicas to 6 if p95 sustains.

oncall-bot: Reminder: scheduled prune-job will run at 03:00 UTC (tickets: PRUNE-412). Last run duration 4m, increased I/O observed.

Maria C: Action items for Ashwin: 1) Watch the router p95 and 5xx rate for first 2 hours. 2) If kv-cache evictions > 500/min, open a ticket and scale cache by +1. 3) If another latency spike like tonight’s, rollback canary and contact Lina for rollback note. 4) Post any config changes in #eng-oncall with the rollback command used.

Ashwin R: Will do. One question: should I pre-scale cache now or wait?

Lina S: I’d hold unless evictions keep trending up. Pre-scaling will increase cost and we only saw sustained evictions after sustained 30% higher tail traffic. If you see a sharp spike, scale immediately.

Jeff K: Also — watch the external embedding service (embeddings-ext). It had a short 502 window at 20:18 that correlated with router retries. If embeddings-ext degrades, we fallback to cached embeddings; otherwise expect more retries.

Maria C: Thanks team. I’ve posted the recent canary logs to the runbook page: https://confluence/redwood/runbooks/oncall/router-canary. Marking handoff complete — feel free to DM if you need anything. :wave:
